questions.questionText: In which direction is the campsite from the lake?
questions.correctAnswer: Northeast
questions.explanation: The campsite is above and to the right of the lake, which is northeast.

questions.questionText: Which grid square contains the museum?
questions.correctAnswer: C2
questions.explanation: The museum is in column C and row 2, giving grid reference C2.

curriculum.objective: Use compass directions, grid references, keys and simple scale to locate and describe places.

questions.questionText: A map scale says 1 cm represents 2 km. What real distance does 4 cm represent?
questions.correctAnswer: 8 km
questions.explanation: Multiplying 4 centimetres by 2 kilometres per centimetre gives 8 kilometres.

curriculum.objective: Use compass directions, grid references, keys and simple scale to locate and describe places.

questions.questionText: Why does a map need a key?
options: To list every person in the area
To explain what its symbols represent
questions.correctAnswer: To explain what its symbols represent
questions.explanation: A key allows readers to connect map symbols with real features.

curriculum.objective: Use compass directions, grid references, keys and simple scale to locate and describe places.

questions.questionText: Which month recorded the greatest rainfall?
questions.correctAnswer: April
questions.explanation: April has the tallest rainfall bar on the chart.

curriculum.objective: Read weather evidence and describe key processes and stores in the water cycle.

questions.questionText: Which process is shown by arrow X?
questions.correctAnswer: Condensation
questions.explanation: Arrow X shows water vapour cooling and forming clouds, which is condensation.

curriculum.objective: Read weather evidence and describe key processes and stores in the water cycle.

questions.questionText: Which instrument measures air temperature?
questions.correctAnswer: Thermometer
questions.explanation: A thermometer measures temperature, usually in degrees Celsius.

curriculum.objective: Read weather evidence and describe key processes and stores in the water cycle.

questions.questionText: Why can two places at the same latitude have different rainfall?
options: Mountains prevent all clouds from forming
Relief and prevailing winds can affect rising air
questions.correctAnswer: Relief and prevailing winds can affect rising air
questions.explanation: Mountains and wind direction influence where air rises, cools and releases rain.

curriculum.objective: Read weather evidence and describe key processes and stores in the water cycle.

questions.questionText: Where is sediment most likely to be deposited in the river diagram?
options: At the inside of the bend
questions.correctAnswer: At the inside of the bend
questions.explanation: Water flows more slowly on the inside of a bend, so it deposits more sediment there.

curriculum.objective: Recognise physical features and explain simple processes that shape rivers, coasts and environments.

questions.questionText: Which environment has very low rainfall, hot days and sparse vegetation?
questions.correctAnswer: Desert
questions.explanation: Very low rainfall, hot days and sparse vegetation are characteristic of a desert.

curriculum.objective: Recognise physical features and explain simple processes that shape rivers, coasts and environments.

questions.questionText: What is erosion?
options: The planting of crops in rows
The daily change from light to dark
The wearing away and removal of rock or soil
questions.correctAnswer: The wearing away and removal of rock or soil
questions.explanation: Erosion wears away material and transports it from its original location.

curriculum.objective: Recognise physical features and explain simple processes that shape rivers, coasts and environments.

questions.questionText: Why are mangrove forests valuable along some tropical coasts?
options: They remove all salt from the ocean
They prevent any organism from living nearby
Their roots reduce wave energy and provide habitats
questions.correctAnswer: Their roots reduce wave energy and provide habitats
questions.explanation: Dense roots slow water, trap sediment and create nursery habitats for many species.

curriculum.objective: Recognise physical features and explain simple processes that shape rivers, coasts and environments.

questions.questionText: Which site is most suitable for a new health clinic?
questions.correctAnswer: Site B
questions.explanation: Site B is close to most homes and beside the main road without occupying the floodplain.

curriculum.objective: Describe settlement patterns, population movement and how transport and services connect places.

questions.questionText: On a transport flow map, what does a thicker arrow usually represent?
options: A larger number of people travelling
questions.correctAnswer: A larger number of people travelling
questions.explanation: Flow maps commonly use arrow thickness to show the relative number of travellers.

curriculum.objective: Describe settlement patterns, population movement and how transport and services connect places.

questions.questionText: Which is a pull factor encouraging people to move to a town?
options: Access to more jobs and services
questions.correctAnswer: Access to more jobs and services
questions.explanation: Employment and services attract people, so they are pull factors.

curriculum.objective: Describe settlement patterns, population movement and how transport and services connect places.

questions.questionText: A village grows beside a road junction. What is the most likely reason?
options: Junctions remove the need for services
Trade only occurs far from routes
The junction improves movement and trade
questions.correctAnswer: The junction improves movement and trade
questions.explanation: Accessible routes help people, goods and services meet, supporting settlement growth.

curriculum.objective: Describe settlement patterns, population movement and how transport and services connect places.

questions.questionText: Which waste category should the school target first?
questions.correctAnswer: Food waste
questions.explanation: Food waste forms the largest section of the audit chart.

curriculum.objective: Use field evidence to compare places and make sustainable decisions about resources and environments.

questions.questionText: Which route causes the least disturbance to the woodland?
options: All routes cross the same area
questions.correctAnswer: Route C
questions.explanation: Route C follows the existing edge path and avoids the woodland core and nesting area.

curriculum.objective: Use field evidence to compare places and make sustainable decisions about resources and environments.

questions.questionText: Why should pupils count traffic at the same time on different days?
options: To ensure every vehicle is identical
To stop weather from ever changing
To make the observations more comparable
questions.correctAnswer: To make the observations more comparable
questions.explanation: Using the same time controls one source of variation and makes daily results easier to compare.

curriculum.objective: Use field evidence to compare places and make sustainable decisions about resources and environments.

questions.questionText: Which action is the most sustainable use of water at school?
options: Use drinking water to wash empty paths daily
Repair leaks and collect rainwater for gardens
questions.correctAnswer: Repair leaks and collect rainwater for gardens
questions.explanation: Preventing waste and using captured rainwater reduces demand on treated water supplies.

curriculum.objective: Use field evidence to compare places and make sustainable decisions about resources and environments.
